title: Heavenly Secrets Inheritance
next_chapter_hook: As the fourth page of the Tianji Record fully manifested, Mo Xiansheng's voice exploded beside Chen Ji's ear—the Seventh Heavenly Fate Fragment lies hidden within the core of the Heavenly Divine Eye.

text.content: The Void trembled, golden runes coiling around Chen Ji like chains. Mo Xiansheng's form condensed within the light, no longer bearing his kind appearance of a fragmented soul—his pupils churned with chaos, and on his brow center was赫然烙印着一道与天机录同源的印记。"A deal?" Mo Xiansheng sneered, "Does a wretch like you even qualify?" Chen Ji felt a vast pressure bearing down, as if ten thousand mountains were crushing his limbs and bones. Cold sweat instantly soaked his back, yet within this extreme oppression, an eerie calm surged in his heart. Negotiation? He never expected it to succeed. He was merely waiting—for this moment, to force Mo Xiansheng to reveal his true trump card.

Chen Ji gritted his teeth, allowing the pressure to bend his spine until it creaked, yet on his face he forced out a smile more tragic than crying. "The junior naturally does not qualify." His voice was hoarse and humble, "But since you have set up this Fragment inheritance, surely it's not merely to crush an ant?" Before the words finished, he suddenly gripped the Tianji Record Fragment tightly. A blurry image flashed through his mind—this was the foresight he had purchased with 5 points of Heavenly Fate: in three breaths, Mo Xiansheng's pressure would have an imperceptible gap. Chen Ji repeated this in his heart three times, then raised his head, his eyes now bearing a resolve. "If the senior wishes to destroy this Tianji Record, go ahead." He smiled even more humbly, "Unfortunately, you wouldn't survive either."

dialogue.content: "Threatening me?" Mo Xiansheng's pupils contracted sharply, a dangerous glint flickering through those chaotic-colored eyes. His pressure surged again. Chen Ji felt his bones creaking, as if the next moment he would be crushed to pieces. Yet just then—he saw it. Chen Ji saw the flash of hesitation in Mo Xiansheng's eyes, saw his brow center mark dimming by half. The gap. Right now. He slammed the Fragment against his chest, meeting that pressure in an almost self-destructive posture. Blood seeped from his seven orifices, dyeing the runes on the Fragment crimson. "Chen Ji today stakes everything on this single gamble!" he roared.

text.content: The Fragment erupted with blinding golden light, resonating with the mark on Mo Xiansheng's brow center. That connection maintained for who knows how many years, under Chen Ji's madness of using blood as the guide and life as the stake, was finally forcibly activated. Mo Xiansheng's expression changed dramatically. He wanted to withdraw his pressure, yet found his fragmented soul being drawn by an irresistible force, merging with the Fragment. "You madman!" Mo Xiansheng howled, "Do you know how much of your lifespan this will cost!" Chen Ji bled from seven orifices, yet his consciousness was terrifyingly clear. Of course he knew. Every glimpse of the future consumed Heavenly Fate, and forcibly activating the inheritance—his price was one-third of his lifespan. But compared to these, there was something else he cared about even more.

Golden runes peeled from the Fragment, stroke by stroke, merging into Chen Ji's Mental Sea. It felt like someone using a burning hot iron rod to carve words upon his soul. Pain. Pain enough to drive him nearly insane. Yet Chen Ji bit down hard on his tongue, anchoring himself to the edge of consciousness with that taste of blood. He was waiting. Waiting for the moment when the fourth page fully unlocked. Mo Xiansheng's furious roar gradually changed to exclamations, then from exclamations to silence. When the final thread of golden light entered Chen Ji's brow center, he felt it—the Tianji Record was complete. Four pages merged as one, a torrent of information like a breaching dam rushed into his consciousness. Countless images came flooding: the founding of the Tianji Pavilion, the falls of generations of prophets, the existence known as the "Heavenly Divine Eye"... And most importantly—the method to break the Deadly Calamity.

Chen Ji knelt on the ground, trembling all over, yet let out a suppressed burst of mad laughter to the sky. The method to break the Deadly Calamity, he had finally found it. However, when that information fully digested, his laughter stopped abruptly. The method was simple—gather the seven Heavenly Fate Fragments, merge them into oneself, and break the shackles of fate. But the problem was... He looked down at his own hands, at the three faintly glowing marks—one from the Fragment obtained upon joining, one from Su Qingyao's trust, and one... from the strand of obsession he desperately seized when his sister Chen Nian was taken. Three. He only had three. Four more were needed. And those four... each corresponded to an existence enough to shake the entire cultivation world.

Just then, Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded again, no longer bearing the previous killing intent, only a weariness and... eerie relief? "Your viciousness exceeds what I anticipated." The fragmented soul drifted before Chen Ji, a complex expression appearing on that aged face, "This old man has waited three thousand years, finally encountering a madman who dares to gamble with his own life." Chen Ji wiped the blood from his face, grinning, his smile more tragic than crying. "Is the senior complimenting me?" His voice was hoarse, "But what about the price? How many years do I have left?" Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment, then raised one finger. "One hundred years." He said, "Originally you would have had at least two hundred years of lifespan, now... only one hundred remains."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji froze for an instant, then laughed again, laughing until tears came out. One hundred years. He still had one hundred years. Funny? Of course it was funny. Any normal person would be beating their chest and regretting, yet Chen Ji was different. After his laughter finished, he wiped his eye corner with his sleeve, his eyes，反而亮得吓人。"Enough." He said, "More than enough." One hundred years was sufficient to gather the remaining four Fragments. Sufficient to scheme across the world, pulling down those lofty Great Ones one by one. Sufficient to... find his sister, to wrest her back from the Holy Sect. The fourth page of the Tianji Record slowly unfolded in his Mental Sea, containing not only clues to the seven Fragments but also notes left by generations of prophets. And in the corner of the final page, he saw a row of faint, small characters: The Seventh Heavenly Fate Fragment, hidden within the core of the Heavenly Divine Eye.

text.content: Heavenly Divine Eye. Chen Ji silently repeated these four characters, his knuckles unconsciously tightening. This was an existence repeatedly mentioned in the Tianji Record yet never explained in detail—it was not a person, not a sect, not even a simple force. It was... the will of Heaven. The embodiment of the world's operating rules. And he, Chen Ji, a waste who hadn't even broken through Foundation Building, now had to make enemies of Heaven? He suddenly found it somewhat amusing. Three months ago, he was still a servant disciple without even a Spirit Root, sweeping floors and carrying water daily,，随时可能被任何一个内门弟子踩死。三个月后，他已经站在了命运的棋盘上，手握天机录，肩扛必死劫，眼望天道之眼。变化太快了。快得连他自己都有些恍惚。但恍惚也只是一瞬。他很快收敛了心神，将那些纷乱的念头压下去，抬头看向墨先生。"前辈，"他开口，声音平静得不像是在问一个关乎生死的问题，"那四道碎片，分别在哪里？"

Mo Xiansheng stared at him for a long while, seemingly reassessing this young man's worth. After a moment, he sighed, waved his hand, and four light images appeared before Chen Ji. The first, in the hands of the Holy Sect's Saintess Ye Qing of the Demonic Path—precisely, within the "Heavenly Fate Lock Core" implanted in her body by the Holy Sect. The second, deep within the bloodline of Xuanwu Sect's number one genius Han Lie, obtained through a secret method from ancient ruins. The third, in the Mental Sea of Tianqing Sect's old Sect Master Ling Yuan, as compensation for his failure in the past to compete for the Tianji Record inheritance. The fourth... Mo Xiansheng's voice paused, his expression becoming peculiar. The fourth was within the Heavenly Fate Lock Key taken by the Demonic Holy Sect three months ago. And that Lock Key had a name—Chen Nian. Chen Ji's younger sister. "So," Chen Ji's voice was very light, almost inaudible, "my sister carries a Fragment?" Mo Xiansheng nodded. "Not just one." He said, "She is the Heavenly Fate Lock Key itself, formed from the most core Fragment among the seven—the Seventh Fragment—condensed."

Chen Ji did not speak. He merely stood there quietly, head bowed, looking at his blood-stained hands. In his Mental Sea, the Tianji Record's contents surged again, a piece of information deliberately sealed away surfacing: The Heavenly Fate Lock Key is the vessel used by generations of prophets to seal the Heavenly Divine Eye. When the seal loosens, the Lock Key will be eroded by the Heavenly Divine Eye's power, gradually losing its self-awareness, ultimately becoming its puppet. And the Holy Sect taking Chen Nian was no coincidence. They were chess pieces manipulated by the Heavenly Divine Eye, their purpose being to make the Fragment within Chen Nian... completely awaken. Chen Ji slowly raised his head. His gaze was still calm, calm as stagnant water. Yet within that dead water's depths, something was burning. "I understand." He said, his voice light yet carrying a chilling intent that made spines tingle, "So I've been driven to a dead end." Four Fragments, belonging to four unshakeable forces. And the fourth is still inside my sister. "To get it back," he laughed, his smile more tragic than crying, "either destroy the Demonic Holy Sect, or... let my sister die."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji clenched his fists, the Tianji Record's information churning in his Mental Sea. He faced a difficult choice—four Fragments, four possibilities. What do you want him to do?

choices.description: Time is tight, and his sister could be devoured by the Heavenly Divine Eye at any moment. Even knowing it's like an egg striking a rock, he must fight desperately. Start with Ye Qing—she is the only ally with a chance of being swayed.
choices.visible_cost: Consume massive Heavenly Fate Value for foresight, revealing some trump cards
choices.visible_reward: Prioritize protecting his sister, strive for alliance with Ye Qing
choices.risk_hint: Exposing strength too early may attract the attention of Ling Yuan and the Heavenly Divine Eye
choices.process_label: 立即行动，优先保护妹妹

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the churning emotions in his chest. Anger? That is the most useless thing. Anxiety? That is even more digging one's own grave. He raised his head, showing Mo Xiansheng a smile more tragic than crying. "Senior, I choose the first path." His voice was very calm, "My sister is in the Holy Sect's hands; every moment delayed is another step toward the abyss. Regarding Ye Qing, I'm confident in persuading her." Saying this, he took out the Tianji Record Fragment from his怀中，一段模糊的预见画面在脑海中浮现——那是三天后，夜清会独自出现在天青宗外的荒野，与圣宗派来的"护道者"发生争执。机会。就是那个时候。

Mo Xiansheng looked at him, a complex light flickering in his eyes. "Have you thought this through?" he asked, "The Demonic Holy Sect is no pushover, and that girl Ye Qing is even more ruthless—" "Senior," Chen Ji interrupted him, his lips curving into a derisive arc, "If I can't even protect my own sister, what right do I have to speak of breaking the Deadly Calamity?" He paused, then added, "Besides..." His voice dropped, audible only to himself, "I promised her I would bring her home." That was a very, very long time ago, before the dilapidated old house in Chen Village, a little girl with pigtails pulling at his clothes, saying in her childish voice: "Brother, can we never be apart?" He had promised. So, even if he had to trample the entire Demonic Holy Sect, he would bring Chen Nian back.

choices.description: Cannot act rashly. The Holy Sect is powerful; rushing into action will only alert the enemy. First use the Tianji Record to continue scheming, silently accumulate strength, and make plans when Ling Yuan shows weakness. Sister... wait a bit longer.
choices.visible_cost: Every day of delay increases the risk of my sister being eroded by one point
choices.visible_reward: Strive for more scheming time, unite allies such as Su
choices.risk_hint: The guilt toward his sister will gradually accumulate in his heart, possibly affecting his mind.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and slowly exhaled. Anger, anxiety, guilt... all his emotions were forcibly pressed into the deepest corner of his heart, transforming into a cold flame burning within. "I choose the second path." He opened his eyes, his voice calm as if discussing someone else's affairs. "The Holy Sect is powerful, and Ye Qing is no easy opponent either. Charging in now would only mean death." He glanced at Mo Xiansheng, a trace of mockery curling at the corner of his lips. "Didn't you say that old thing Ling Yuan also has a fragment? Then we'll start from him." The mantis stalks the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind. Chen Ji never minded being that least conspicuous oriole. Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, then suddenly laughed. "Good." He said, "This old man has waited three thousand years, finally encountering someone who can stay composed."

Just then, the fourth page of the Tianji Record suddenly burst forth with dazzling light. The complete inheritance content was finally fully unlocked, countless pieces of information surging into Chen Ji's Mental Sea like a tide. However, as those pieces of information gradually clarified, Chen Ji's expression changed. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again, no longer carrying killing intent, only exhaustion and...诡异的欣慰？"Your ruthlessness exceeds my expectations." The remnant soul drifted slowly before Chen Ji, that aged face showing a complex expression. "This old man has waited three thousand years, finally encountering a madman who dares to bet his own life." Chen Ji wiped the blood from his face, grinning, his smile more like crying. "Is the senior complimenting me?" His voice was hoarse. "So what's the price? How many years do I have left?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, then raised one finger. "A hundred years." He said, "Originally you would have had at least two hundred years of lifespan. Now... only one hundred remains."

The fourth page of the Tianji Record unfolded completely, countless runes flowing like water through Chen Ji's consciousness. He saw the lives of prophetic seers throughout the ages, witnessed their tragic or wretched endings, and uncovered a truth deliberately buried—the Heavenly Eye was not an incarnation of the Heavenly Dao, but a collection of grudges from the "First Prophet" cleaved away by the Heavenly Dao. It treated all living beings as chess pieces and prophets as its pawns, attempting to devour the Heavenly Dao and take its place. And the Tianji Record was merely a tool it used to select "quality vessels." Chen Ji stared at the faintly visible small characters in his Mental Sea: Heavenly Fate Fragment, the Seventh, hidden within the core of the Heavenly Eye. His pupils constricted sharply. The Seventh Fragment was in no one's hands. It was inside the Heavenly Eye. And if he wanted to break the Deadly Fate... he would have to—kill the Heavenly Eye. Hah. What irony. Chen Ji, a废物 who hadn't even broken through Foundation Building, now had to make an enemy of "Heaven."

Chen Ji suddenly burst into laughter, the sound echoing through the vast Mental Sea, stirring up golden ripples. "Interesting." He said, "Absolutely goddamn interesting." He had thought the so-called Deadly Fate was merely a curse, a small obstacle that could be easily broken by collecting fragments. And the result? Fragments scattered across the hands of four major forces, while the most crucial one was actually inside the Heavenly Eye. In other words, he would not only have to become enemies with the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, Xuanwu Sect, and Tianqing Sect, but also with the entire Heavenly Dao's rules. Mad. This world had gone mad. But Chen Ji... laughed. Not bitter laughter, not cold laughter, but a genuine, nearly manic roar of laughter. Since Heaven wanted to play with him, he would play along. Since fate wanted to crush him, he would defy destiny and change his fate. After all, he had nothing left to lose. A hundred years of lifespan, three fragments, an incomplete Tianji Record, plus a "废物" reputation. These cards were enough for him to overturn the entire chessboard.

After laughing, Chen Ji sat cross-legged again, spreading the Tianji Record across his lap. In the Mental Sea, that complete "Seven Fragments Distribution Map" clearly presented itself before his eyes. The First Fragment, he already possessed. The Second, within Ye Qing—precisely, the "Heavenly Fate Lock Core" implanted by the Holy Sect in her chest. The Third, deep within Han Lie's bloodline, obtained three months ago from an ancient ruins he stumbled upon. The Fourth, deep within the Mental Sea of the old Tianqing Sect Master Ling Yuan—that was the "compensation" the Tianji Record gave him after his failed attempt at the Tianji Record inheritance. The Fifth, in the hands of a certain Supreme Elder of the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path. The Sixth, within the inheritance of a certain reclusive Ancestor of the Xuanwu Sect. As for the Seventh... Chen Ji stared at those small characters, his gaze gradually deepening. "Senior," he suddenly spoke, "If I collect all seven fragments simultaneously, what would happen?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a very long time. When he spoke again, his voice carried a gravity Chen Ji had never heard before: "In theory, you could replace the Heavenly Eye and become the new 'Heavenly Dao Will.'"

Replace the Heavenly Dao Will. Chen Ji chewed those five characters over and over in his heart. It sounded tempting. Control the Heavenly Dao, manipulate fate, overlook all beings... Perhaps any ordinary person hearing this proposal would go mad on the spot. But Chen Ji didn't. He merely淡淡地 said "Oh," then asked: "And the price?" Mo Xiansheng froze, seemingly not expecting him to be so direct. "The price?" he repeated. "Tell me the price." Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze calm. "There are no free lunches in this world, especially lunches related to 'Heaven.' What is the price of becoming the Heavenly Dao Will?" Mo Xiansheng fell silent. A very long silence. When he spoke again, there was an undetectable tremor in his voice: "You will lose all emotions as a 'person.' Joy, sorrow, anger, fear... all will be stripped away. You will become a puppet of the Heavenly Dao, acting according to the will of 'Rules' rather than your own will." Chen Ji nodded, a trace of mockery curling at the corner of his lips. "So I'd become another Heavenly Eye, essentially." He said, "Thank you for the warning, senior. This Heavenly Dao isn't worth having."

Mo Xiansheng froze. He looked at this blood-soaked, dispirited young man before him, suddenly noticing there was not a trace of hesitation in his eyes—only a cold, clear-headed composure. "You... don't want to become a god?" he asked, disbelief evident in his voice. Chen Ji tilted his head, a playful smile spreading across his features. "What's so good about becoming a god?" He said, "Sitting up in heaven all day, coldly watching the ants below fight head-over-heels for pills and martial techniques? Watching your loved ones grow old and die one by one, yet unable to feel any emotional波动?" He stood up, dusting off his clothes. "Senior, I Chen Ji am a mortal. I don't want to become a god, nor do I want to be the Heavenly Dao. I only want..." His voice paused, a tenderness flashing through his eyes that others couldn't comprehend. "To take my sister home and let her live safely. As for the Deadly Fate, the Heavenly Eye—" He coldly smiled. "They're just stones blocking the road. Kick them away. If you can't kick them, go around. If you can't go around..." His gaze deepened. "Then blow them up."

As Chen Ji's words fell, a strange vibration suddenly resonated through the Mental Sea. On the fourth page of the Tianji Record, those originally static runes began to flow, sketching a blurry image in the Void—that was the core of the Heavenly Eye, an abyss as black as ink, with a faint white light flickering at its center. That was... Chen Nian. Su Qingyao had said the Heavenly Fate Lock Key was the key to sealing the Heavenly Eye. The Holy Sect took Chen Nian away, ostensibly coveting the power within her, but actually under the Heavenly Eye's backstage manipulation—it needed the Lock Key to complete its final awakening. And that white light within Chen Nian was precisely the core of the seal. Once the awakening completed, Chen Nian's consciousness would be completely erased, becoming nourishment for the Heavenly Eye's rebirth. "Time is running out." Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly sounded. "According to the Tianji Record's calculations, the Lock Key's awakening has at most three months. After three months, your sister will completely disappear." Chen Ji stared at that mass of white light, his knuckles white from clenching. Three months. Ninety days. How much time did he have left to waste?

In the Mental Sea, the fourth page of the Tianji Record suddenly burst forth with dazzling light. The complete inheritance content was finally fully unlocked, countless pieces of information surging into Chen Ji's consciousness like a tide. He saw the lives of prophetic seers throughout the ages, witnessed their tragic or wretched endings, and uncovered a truth deliberately buried—the Heavenly Eye was not an incarnation of the Heavenly Dao, but a collection of grudges from the "First Prophet" cleaved away by the Heavenly Dao. It treated all living beings as chess pieces and prophets as its pawns, attempting to devour the Heavenly Dao and take its place. And the Tianji Record was merely a tool it used to select "quality vessels." Chen Ji stared at the faintly visible small characters in his Mental Sea: Heavenly Fate Fragment, the Seventh, hidden within the core of the Heavenly Eye. His pupils constricted sharply. The Seventh Fragment was in no one's hands. It was inside the Heavenly Eye. And if he wanted to break the Deadly Fate... he would have to—kill the Heavenly Eye.
